title: From Hourly Rates to Annual Salary: How to Convert Your Pay, Including the Oscar Piastri Salary Example
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using the standard 38‑hour week. We explain tax, super, and casual loading, with a look at the Oscar Piastri salary for context.
salarySummary: Based on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38‑hour week, the annual gross pay is approximately $52,254.88.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full‑time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $26.44 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $52,254.88 per year. This is the gross annual figure before tax and other deductions.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the National Minimum Wage receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For the minimum wage of $26.44 per hour, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave that casuals do not receive. When converting to annual pay, use the loaded rate if you are a casual employee.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at a rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your gross pay. For example, on a $52,254.88 annual salary, the super contribution would be $6,270.59, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is an additional benefit, not part of your take‑home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to an Annual Salary

Whether you are negotiating a job offer or comparing pay across industries, understanding how an hourly rate translates into an annual salary is essential. The standard formula used in Australia is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For most full‑time roles, we assume a 38‑hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This gives you a gross annual figure before tax, the Medicare levy, and other deductions.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. For a 38‑hour week, the weekly pay is $1,004.90, and the annual gross pay is $52,254.88. If you are paid fortnightly, simply double the weekly amount: $2,009.80.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most employees, however, are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates. Award wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026, as confirmed by the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides. You can check your specific award rate using the [pay guides](/blog) or the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. When converting to an annual figure, use the loaded rate if you are a casual. Remember: never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into a calculator that adds it again. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains this further.

## Tax and the Medicare Levy

Once you have your gross annual salary, you need to estimate your take‑home pay. For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian Taxation Office’s resident tax rates are:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. For a full‑time worker on the National Minimum Wage ($52,254.88), the estimated tax would be approximately $5,092 plus the Medicare levy of $1,045, leaving a take‑home pay of around $46,118. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

## Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions on your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12%, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your salary; it is an additional payment into your super fund. For the minimum wage example, the employer would contribute $6,270.59 per year on top of your gross pay. This is separate from your take‑home pay and is designed for your retirement.

## Applying the Conversion to Any Salary

The same formula works for any hourly rate, whether you are earning the minimum wage or a high‑profile income like the Oscar Piastri salary. While Oscar Piastri’s exact earnings as a Formula 1 driver are not publicly confirmed in detail, the principle of converting an annual figure to an hourly rate applies to any income. For instance, if a driver earns $5 million per year, dividing by 52 weeks and then by 38 hours gives an hourly equivalent of approximately $2,531. This highlights how the hourly‑to‑annual conversion can be used to compare pay across vastly different roles.

### Fortnightly and Monthly Comparisons

Many employers pay fortnightly or monthly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For monthly, multiply your weekly pay by 52 and divide by 12. These figures help you budget and compare job offers. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page provides more examples.

## Important Considerations

The annual figure calculated here assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a gross estimate. For award‑covered employees, penalty rates and allowances can significantly change your actual pay. Always refer to your specific award or agreement. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool provides personalised rates.

Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is based on the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Summary

Converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a standard full‑time role, use 38 hours. Remember to distinguish between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and super paid on top. Whether you are checking the Oscar Piastri salary or your own pay, this method gives you a clear picture of your gross annual earnings. For more detailed calculations, explore our [reference tables](/data) and other resources.
